agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading
COVID-19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s
Order (revised December 16, 2021). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by
roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will
be live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during
the meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item you would
like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference to
be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as states
of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, State of California, and a federal emergency
declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission
meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to
the health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the
same place.
The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3)
minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. You
must first sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://MalibuCity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the
directions for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.
Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.
Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the
Consent Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been
submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no
final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in
the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing MLinden@MalibuCity.org.
The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].
I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 30th day of December 2021, at 12:00 p.m.

ITEM 1.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Hans Laetz provided an update on the KBUU radio station signal expansion project. He
  stated Alert FM testing was scheduled to begin next week. He discussed problems with
  the County of Los Angeles plan to use NOAA radios discussed in its presentation to the
  City Council last night.

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Manager Dueñas discussed the Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS)
  last week. She stated the City’s major concern was residents not being able to call
  911 in an emergency. She discussed actions taken by cell service providers to
  provide backup power. She stated Southern California Edison (SCE) provided
  resiliency packs to residents on Thanksgiving Day at Bluffs Park. In response to
  Mr. Laetz, she agreed FM Alert seemed the best option for the City. She stated
  she would continue to monitor and follow up with the County on its all-weather
  alert and follow up with them. Keep you posted

  She stated the parking citation fine schedule would come back for further review
  with input from the Finance Department and the City’s Hearing Officer. She
  stated there were concerns some of the recommended increases may not
  defensible.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated the City was preparing for the County’s
  Homeless Count on January 26, 2022. He stated volunteers were being recruited.

  Fire Safety Liaison Brossard stated the City and most of Los Angeles County
  fared well during the recent Red Flag Warning and significant Santa Ana wind
  event. He discussed a small fire near Tuna Canyon on Sunday evening. He stated
  Live Fuel Moistures were up from 60 to 74 due to recent rains and marine layer.
  He stated it was expected to go down in coming weeks. He reported the City
  Council accepted the CalFire grant at last night’s meeting. He discussed the status
  of tree removal using funds from the Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy grant.
  He stated 36 trees were removed since November 6.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed the City’s activities to prepare in
  advance for impacts of the PSPS, including deployment of changeable message
  signs (CMS) and generators to provide backup power to traffic signals. He stated
  crews were on standby and were dispatched at 2:00 a.m. on Thanksgiving to clear
  fallen trees and debris caused from canyons and city roads. He stated damaged
  signs and signals are being repaired with completion expected by the end of the
  week. He suggested a refresher on use of radios and consolidation of radio
  signals.

  Executive Assistant Linden announced Brown Act training for all commissioners
  would be offered on Friday, December 10, 1:30 to 3:30 p.m. She encouraged all
  commissioners to attend.

  Vice Chair Stewart requested City staff report on what was learned in the recent
  PSPS.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated radios were a better communication tool
  but needed to be set up better.

  Public Safety Manager Dueñas stated the City needed to know more about
  services and resources available from SCE and help identify people who needed
  power for medical devices. She stated staff would continue to work with cell
  service providers to ensure that backup power was added to their equipment.

  Fire Safety Liaison Brossard discussed how Public Safety staff could be a
  communication liaison between City staff and the Fire Department. He stated it
  might be good to have staff in the City during Red Flag Warnings.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores agreed with Public Safety Manager Dueñas and Fire
  Safety Liaison Brossard that the City could be more proactive about notifying
  residents about services available when the power goes out.

ITEM 1.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Commissioner Gibbs stated he did not receive any message prior to the power
  going out. Public Safety Manager Dueñas stated the City sent utility advisories for
  power outages and PSPS. In response to Commissioner Gibbs, Public Safety
  Manager Dueñas explained the process for SCE to notify the City about PSPS.
  Commissioner Gibbs stated there needed to be better communication resources
  for residents. He suggested there be a hotlink for individuals with special needs to
  be directed to service information.

  Vice Chair Stewart thanked Public Safety Manager Dueñas and Hans Laetz for
  the presentation at last night’s City Council meeting regarding indoor warning
  systems. He stated the City needed to focus on alerting the population and
  advising them what to do. He thanked Commissioner Gibbs, Ex Officio Member
  Woodworth and Richard Garvey for their assistance. He commended Public
  Works Director DuBoux and Public Works staff for their proactive efforts to
  ensure there was backup power for traffic signals. He stated the generators needed
  to last more than four hours. He stated SCE offered rebates up to $500 per
  generator. He stated the CERT radio system worked throughout the windstorm.
  He discussed HAM radios licensed in the City. He stated he observed wires
  blowing in the wind last week and the PSPS may have prevented a fire from
  starting. He suggested looking for grant funds for the FM Alert system.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated he was 40 hours without power from
  Wednesday to Friday. He expressed concern about the loss of hardwired landlines
  and the inability to call 911. He stated communication was completely
  unavailable for 16 hours in the canyon areas. He suggested discussing with

  Frontier and SCE to ensure they were coordinating with each other. He
  commended the Fire Department for staging resources in advance. He stated SCE
  needed to be more proactive about educating the public about what they can do to
  prepare for a fire or power outage. He asked if the City considered a soft opening
  of its Emergency Operations Center (EOC).

  Public Safety Manager Dueñas explained the City’s procedures regarding when to
  activate the EOC. She stated the Council had directed the Public Safety

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated community fire brigade training continued.
  He stated an onsite walkthrough in Hidden Hills was scheduled for December 11.

  Commissioner Gibbs expressed concern about communication during the wind

  repeater during an emergency. He suggested a repeater be placed on Catalina for
  brigades to communicate with each other.

  Commissioner Anneet stated she was surprised her landline did not work. She
  suggested emergency alerts be sent for power outages. She stated it was critical
  that generators for cell service be working. She thanked Public Works for
  ensuring there was backup power for traffic signals. She stated the City needed to
  stay on SCE, Verizon, and Frontier about ensuring backup generators were
  working.

  Vice Chair Stewart stated telecommunication companies were converting hardline
  services to Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP).

  Fire Safety Liaison Brossard stated cordless telephones would not work without

  Commissioner Anneet stated that was the type of information that needed to be
  included in the City’s education.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated he was happy with progress made on traffic signals.
  He stated he would like to explore allowing CERT, Arson Watch, or other civilian
  volunteers to set generators in place. He announced the crime mapping software
  had been activated. Public Safety Manager Dueñas stated the requested crime map
  through LexisNexis was not available. Commissioner Spiegel stated the software
  was what the Sheriff’s Department currently utilized and used the same data. He
  stated homeless individuals were moving back to the Zuma area that was recently
  cleaned out.

  Chair Frost stated Caltrans approval was required for anyone activating generators
  for traffic signal backup power. He discussed wires that went down in the recent
  wind event. He stated that could have caused a fire if the wires had been
  energized. He stated the inconvenience of a power outage was worth avoiding a
  fire. He expressed disappointment with how abusive residents were toward SCE
  workers. He stated he looked forward to hearing how individuals defended
  themselves against parking tickets they deserved. He thanked the Public Works
  crews for a great job last week. He discussed why undergrounding would help but
  would not solve the problem of power outages.

  In response to Chair Frost, Commissioner Gibbs stated 911 could not be called
  over a radio. He discussed how emergency information could be shared over a
  radio. Ex Officio Member Woodworth discussed how a HAM radio could get
  through to a phone number.

  Vice Chair Stewart discussed how emergency calls can sometimes be placed to

  Commissioner Spiegel suggested the City consider using satellite phones.

  Public Works Director DuBoux provided a presentation with the report. He stated

  suggested the two commissions hold a joint meeting to discuss recommendations.

  Chair Frost agreed with scheduling a joint meeting with the Public Works

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated projects on local City roads were not

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Commission agreed to hear Item No. 4.C. before Item No. 4.B.

  C.  Public Safety Agency Activity
  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and

  Lieutenant Braden discussed the recent arrest of a transient who attacked another
  individual. He encouraged the public to notify the Sheriff’s Department of
  suspicious individuals. He discussed the recent power outage. He agreed more
  people needed to be authorized to install the traffic signal generators. He stated it
  was unacceptable that backup power was not provided by cell service providers to

  Latigo Canyon be considered. He discussed enforcement of motorhomes in the
  City and unincorporated County areas. He stated the Sheriff’s Department was

Subject:  Second Review of Parking Citation Fine Schedule

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Receive a report on parking citation fine implementation
challenges; and 2) Re-evaluate previously recommended parking citation fine increases
and revise the recommendations, if appropriate.

DISCUSSION:  At the November 3, 2021 Public Safety Commission meeting, the
Commission was presented with a number of parking violations to consider for increased
fines. The list of proposed violations was based on input from the Los Angeles County
Sheriff’s Department (LASD) Lost Hills Station and Volunteers on Patrol (VOP). According
to LASD and VOP representatives, the identified violations are those that are frequently
written, pose public safety hazards, and do not appear to have fines that sufficiently deter
the behavior.

After thorough discussion, the Commission voted unanimously to increase the fines for
the following violations as indicated:

Six of the violations were called out for substantial increases to $150 due to their
prevalence and public safety impact.

However, when Public Safety staff subsequently notified Finance staff of the proposed
increases, concerns were raised including the following:

  • The City typically aims to be consistent with the Las Virgenes Parking Authority
  (LVPA) and these recommended increases were not consistent with LVPA
  • Fines that are too high and perceived as disproportionate to the offense have a
  greater chance of being appealed
  • Citation appeals incur additional staff and contractor costs

In addition, it was pointed out that high fines do not guarantee better compliance,
particularly with visitors to the City. If compliance is the goal, better signage and public
education is suggested as a more efficient deterrent.

It is also important to note that in July 2020, the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed in the
case, Pimentel vs. City of Los Angeles, that parking tickets and fees must comply with the
U.S. Constitution Eighth Amendment’s ban on “excessive fines.” The Pimentel vs. City of
Los Angeles case was regarding a $63 parking meter fine. To determine whether the fine
was “grossly disproportional” to the offense, the court looked at four factors:

  1) the nature and extent of the underlying offense
  2) whether the underlying offense related to other illegal activities

  Page 2 of 3
  Agenda Item # 3.A.
   3) whether other penalties may be imposed for the offense
  4) the extent of the harm caused by the offense

Although the Court ultimately ruled that the $63 fine was reasonable, the four factors used
to determine the decision provide a valuable guide.

Staff recommends that the Public Safety Commission consider input from the City’s
Finance Manager and apply the four factors used in the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals case,
Pimentel vs. City of Los Angeles, to determine if the recommended fine increases should
be adjusted.

  COMMUNITY I CRIMINAL ISSUES

 1. We conducted a monthly parental resource class at Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station. This program was developed
by our unit and is designed to educate parents about: 1) The current trends in juvenile behavior and
delinquency, 2) Alcohol/narcotic awareness and recognition, 3) School policy and campus issues, 4) Gang
awareness and negative peer relations, 5) Parental rights and responsibilities and, 6) Parental responses to
incorrigible and/or delinquent behavior. We also address the specific concerns relating to the minor’s behavior.
 We educate the minor and their parents of possible criminal behavior and the legal consequences. We offer
suggestions and make recommendations to improve the minor’s quality of life.

2. Spoke with numerous citizens and parents who called to question various juvenile concerns and issues in the
community. We also provide the parents with various juvenile resource programs within our community.

3. We met with the Sylmar Juvenile Court District Attorney regarding the investigation and filing of criminal
charges against juvenile offenders.

4. Met with Captain Salvador Becerra throughout the month in order to keep him up to date regarding our
unit’s investigations and current juvenile issues within our city.

5. Entered juveniles into the Juvenile Automated Index system for various violations.

6. Made court appearances to testify as witnesses on the part of the People of the State of California and
attended court proceedings in cases generated from the City of Malibu. We also investigated, prepared, and
filed cases with the District Attorney’s office. We additionally assisted other investigators in the preparation of
cases for court.

7. We met with station narcotic detectives on a regular basis to exchange information regarding juvenile and
drug related issues. We have worked with the narcotic detectives on several narcotic cases directly and
indirectly involving juveniles.

MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 5, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED – VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet
  and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Keegan Gibbs

  ALSO PRESENT:  Susan Dueñas, Public Safety Manager; Renée Neermann, Finance
  Manager; Chris Brossard, Fire Safety Liaison; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Arthur
  Aladjadjian, Public Works Superintendent; Sarah Kaplan, Public Safety Specialist;
  Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant; Parker Davis, Media Technician; and
  Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Spiegel led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Stewart moved and Commissioner Spiegel seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Gibbs absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on December 30, 2021.

ITEM 1.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian provided an update on the City’s
  response to last week’s storm event. He stated all roads were now open.

  Vice Chair Stewart requested advice for homeowners on private roads during storm
  events. Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian confirmed City workers would
  not go on private roads. He stated homeowner associations often had contractors
  on call. He stated the Fire Department could assist with downed trees.

  Public Safety Manager Dueflas stated the Governor declared a state of emergency
  for the storms allowing for potential reimbursement of costs for the City’s response.
  She stated the City assisted American Red Cross with setting up a shelter at Malibu
  High School for Leo Carrillo State Beach evacuees. She announced City Hall was
  closed to the public for the rest of January due to a rise in COVID-19 cases. She
  stated staff were still available to provide services. She reminded Commissioners
  they could assist with the Homeless Count on January 26 at 6:30 a.m.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores confirmed the City was working closely with the
  County to get the word out about the Homeless Count.

  Fire Safety Liaison Brossard stated 2021 was a good year for Malibu with only
  about five acres burned within the city limits. He stated fuel moisture levels were
  currently at 79 percent. He stated hazard tree removal continued with 18 properties
  visited, and 38 trees removed, using approximately $88,000 of the $300,000
  budget. He stated the removals would resume next week.

ITEM 1.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth agreed with Fire Safety Liaison Brossard that
  Malibu was lucky in 2021. He commended the Fire Department for being proactive.
  He recommended the City and Fire Department continue efforts to get homeowners
  to address fire risks on their property. He discussed non-profit organizations
  working on fire mitigation. He suggested the City push utilities to provide better
  information about power shutoffs and keeping communication lines open during
  power outages. He suggested businesses along PCH remain open during
  evacuations. He discussed questionable billing charges from water districts.

  Commissioner Anneet stated she observed resources responding to a fire in
  Northern California that were supported by homeowners who ensured defensibility
  of their property. She stated it was important to continue to educate the community
  about defensibility.

  Commissioner Spiegel discussed a slide at Puerco Canyon that shut down the
  highway for a few hours. He stated residents were forced to use canyon roads,
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of January 5, 2022
Page 3 of 6

  which added undue risk. He stated the City needed a better plan to allow traffic
  through on PCH.

  Vice Chair Stewart congratulated Chair Frost for receiving the first public safety
  award from the Malibu Association of Realtors. He stated he and Chair Frost met
  with Interim City Manager McClary, Public Safety Manager Dueflas, and Public
  Works Director DuBoux to discuss the Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) in
  November. He stated they discussed the need for additional generators, more people
  to place generators at traffic signals, backup generators for cell service, and better
  radio options for City staff communication. He stated he attended Brown Act
  training on December 10.

  In response to Vice Chair Stewart, Public Safety Manager Duefias provided an
  update the status of crime mapping and installation of cameras.

  Chair Frost stated the property owner at Las Tunas contracted a weekly patrol for
  his property. He asked what would happen if flooding from a private road spread
  onto public streets. Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian stated City staff
  would contact the property owner to mitigate the problem.

  Chair Frost asked why traffic signals in eastern Malibu went out during the storms.
  Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian stated the City contacted Caltrans and
  was advised that signals had to be reset due to power surges that disabled the
  batteries. In response to Chair Frost, Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian
  stated the City had nearly completed repairing and replacing signs damaged during
  the storms. He stated the City would inform Caltrans of missing or damaged signs

ITEM 3  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Second Review of Parking Citation Fine Schedule

  Recommended Action: 1) Receive a report on parking citation fine implementation
  challenges; and 2) Re-evaluate previously recommended parking citation fine
  increases and revise the recommendations, if appropriate.

  Public Safety Manager Dueñas presented the report. She introduced Renée
  Neermann, Finance Manager.

  Finance Manager Neermann stated raising fines was often not a deterrent since
  people did not know the fine until they received a citation. She discussed common
  reasoning used by people to contest citations, such as confusing signage and
  markings and uncommonly shaped fire hydrants. She stated the vehicle code
  required that fines be similar to those in surrounding jurisdictions. She discussed
  phone calls accusing the City of using citations to raise revenue. She stated the City
  was obligated to provide the option of a payment plan, which required additional
  monitoring by staff or the contractor, which negated the fine.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated he disagreed with this item being brought back to the
  Commission. He stated it was important that Commission recommendations be
  taken straight to the City Council, and staff could comment directly to the Council.
  He stated Malibu was different than Las Virgenes. He stated deterrence was not the
  only consideration. He stated there needed to be punitive measures. He suggested
  presenting the Commission’s original recommendation to the City Council.

  Commissioner Anneet stated surrounding neighborhood fine structures were taken
  into account when this item was originally discussed. She stated most violations
  were obvious. Finance Manager Neermann stated remarks about confusing signage
  were shared with the Public Work Department.

  Public Safety Manager Dueñas stated the staff report attachment displayed fines
  charged by other jurisdictions. In response to Commissioner Anneet, Public Safety
  Manager Dueflas stated Santa Monica’s fines were lower on many of the citations.

  Chair Frost agreed that some signs and markings were unclear. He stated fire

  Vice Chair Stewart stated other cities’ fine schedules were considered. He stated he

  Public Safety Specialist Kaplan stated the LVPA included Agoura Hills, Hidden
  Hills, Westlake Village, and Calabasas.

  Vice Chair Stewart thanked Finance Manager Neermann and the hearing officer for
  their work. He stated none of the LVPA cities were beach cities with millions of
  visitors each year. He discussed the step structure for many County fines. He stated
  Santa Monica had low fines for parking but was extremely aggressive with
  violations related to bike lanes. He stated blocking streets in a high fire risk city
  like Malibu was a greater offense requiring a higher fine. He stated parking citations
  were intended to be penalties, not deterrents.

  In response to Commissioner Spiegel, Public Safety Manager Dueñas stated the
  item was brought back out of respect for the Commission and due to the new

  Chair Frost stated he compared many fines to those imposed by other beach cities,

  about signage or the validity of a fine.

  Finance Manager Neermann stated the City received pushback about how high the

  Commissioner Anneet stated the $150.00 fines were significantly higher than any

  comparable to Manhattan Beach and Newport Beach.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated there were six categories where the
  recommended increased fine was much higher than the comparable fine schedules.

  Chair Frost displayed a photo of a disconnected trailer parked in the PCH median.
